CausalChain: Androgen receptor activation -> Increases PKA/CREB signaling -> Upregulates HK2 expression -> Enhances aerobic glycolysis (Warburg effect) -> Contributes to sorafenib resistance; Concurrently, AR activation -> Downregulates miR-199a-5p -> Loss of HK2 inhibition -> Further boosts glycolysis
Hypothesis: Restoration of miR-199a-5p in AR-driven HCC will suppress HK2-mediated glycolysis, reducing the Warburg effect and thereby overcoming sorafenib resistance.
Abstract: This hypothesis explores the interplay between androgen receptor (AR) signaling and microRNA regulation in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) metabolic reprogramming. Specifically, we propose that AR activation in HCC not only upregulates critical glycolytic enzymes, such as hexokinase 2 (HK2), via pathways like PKA/CREB, but also downregulates miR-199a-5p—a microRNA that normally suppresses HK2 expression. The combined effect leads to an exacerbation of the Warburg effect and contributes to sorafenib resistance. By restoring miR-199a-5p levels, it may be possible to dampen HK2-mediated glycolysis, thereby shifting the metabolic balance toward a state that is more susceptible to sorafenib therapy. This integrated molecular approach provides a promising new avenue to overcome drug resistance and mitigate aggressive tumor growth in HCC.
